Subject: Redwood structured output reliability — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Acme eng team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — appreciate the context on the product search flow and the constraints around deterministic JSON outputs for your UI. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the integration forward: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Backend: Node service that calls LLMs for candidate generation, then a reranker against your vector DB (Pinecone).
- Primary need: stable, schema-conformant JSON outputs for product suggestions (used directly by the UI).
- Scale targets: ~300 rps at peak for search rerank calls; p50 latency target ~150ms.
- Security: must use token-based auth; possibility of VPC/Dedicated if needed for compliance.

Integration topics we discussed to follow up on
1) SDK setup & auth — we’ll share a Node sample that demonstrates Redwood SDK usage with API keys and how to swap to mTLS / Private routing for Dedicated customers.
2) Request routing — options for sending generation vs. reranking to different model variants (latency-optimized vs. accuracy-optimized) and fallback policies.
3) Structured output reliability — JSON schema enforcement, constrained decoding strategies, and server-side validation + retry/repair patterns.
4) Embeddings & reranker flow — pattern to call Redwood for an embeddings-based reranker vs. calling your vector DB + Redwood for final scoring.

Attachments: I attached a suggested schema (acme_structured_schema.json) and a short Node SDK sample (redwood_sdk_sample.ts).

Next steps / asks
- Vivek (SE) to do a 45-min technical walkthrough next week (SDK + schema enforcement + retry patterns). Suggested times: Tue 3/3 10am PT or Wed 3/4 11am PT. Which works for you?
- Alex: can you confirm the sample dataset shape (fields we need in schema) and whether you want the reranker to live inside Redwood or remain in Pinecone?

I’ll put a calendar invite on hold for Tue 3/3 10am PT and we can cancel if needed.

Marissa, Vivek,

Thanks for the clear summary — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side before the walkthrough:

- Schema: the UI expects an array of candidate objects with fields: id (string), title (string), score (float), categories (array[string]), and metadata (kv map). We’d like an optional confidence/confidence_source field we can show on hover.
- Reranker architecture: currently we do nearest-neighbor in Pinecone -> top 50 candidates -> rerank server that calls out to models for final scoring. Ideally we keep Pinecone for vector search but want Redwood to handle the final scoring/rerank call if possible.
- Determinism: we've seen models hallucinate keys or return variants of field names; we need an approach that results in a valid JSON object 99.9% of the time.

Can Vivek include an example of: 1) constrained decoding / function call or schema enforcement; 2) a validation + retry pattern we can run server-side if the model output violates the schema (e.g., fix-up prompt + second attempt)? Also please confirm whether Redwood has built-in reranker recipes or if we should implement scoring logic client-side after getting model outputs.

Any of the suggested times next week work for me — Tue 3/3 10am PT is preferred.

Thanks,
Alex

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Redwood structured output reliability — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex — quick technical notes ahead of the walkthrough. Will cover these live but wanted to leave a written summary you can reference.

High-level recommendations
1) Auth & SDK: use Redwood SDK with API keys for hosted. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys + optional mTLS. In Node: set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; sample in attached redwood_sdk_sample.ts.

2) Routing & reranker pattern:
- Keep Pinecone for vector search (NN search -> top N candidates).
- Send top N to Redwood generate endpoint (or a lightweight reranker model in Redwood) for re-scoring.
- If throughput/latency is critical, use a small accuracy-optimized reranker (quantized) pinned on Dedicated for predictable p95.

3) Structured output enforcement options (in order of reliability):
- Function calling / tool calling (preferred when you can map fields to discrete types): declare a function signature that mirrors the schema so the model returns structured params.
- Constrained decoding + JSON schema enforcement: Redwood supports model-side constrained decoding to reduce token-level errors (e.g., disallow unknown field names).
- Post-response validation with repair: parse the returned JSON server-side and run a deterministic "repair" prompt that prepends the broken JSON and asks the model to return a corrected JSON matching the schema.

4) Validation + retry pattern (recommended resilient flow):
- Step A: Call Redwood generate with structured-output constraints (highest chance of valid JSON).
- Step B: Attempt to parse the response; if parse OK and passes schema validator, accept.
- Step C: If parse fails or missing critical fields, call a short repair prompt including the schema + original output and ask for corrected JSON (set low temperature and small token budget).
- Step D: If repair attempt fails twice, fall back to a deterministic server-side heuristic (e.g., map fields from nearest tokens) and flag for human review.

5) Observability & SLAs: instrument token-level latency and schema-failure rate in Redwood Console. We can create an alert if schema-failure rate > 0.1% over 10k requests.

Example schema suggestion: (attached acme_structured_schema.json) — top-level object {"candidates": [ {"id":"string","title":"string","score":"number","categories":["string"],"confidence":"number","metadata":{"key":"value"}} ] }

We also have a reranker recipe that takes embeddings + candidate text and returns a normalized score; Vivek will demo both approaches (Redwood-hosted reranker vs. client-side scoring after model output) in the walkthrough.

I’ll include a short Node snippet in the meeting that shows: SDK init, constrained decoding call, parse+validate logic, and a repair retry.

Marissa — I’ll take Tue 3/3 10am PT. Putting the invite on the calendar now.
